Hydrologic Monitoring Program
Westmoreland Resources initiated a preliminary surface water monitoring program within the project area in April, 1973. The program was later expanded to include ground-water quality observations and additional surface water stations were added in March, 1975. The program is designed to obtain baseline chemical and physical characteristics of the surface and ground water in and around Tracts II and III (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1). It has been operating during the first phases of mining in Tract III and will continue through the duration of mining operations.
Figures D-1 and D-2 show that locations of the surface and ground water monitoring stations established by Westmoreland Resources and their consultants. The stations are concentrated on or near Sarpy Creek, with a few in other parts of Tracts III and II. CT&E locations 1 through 8 have been sampled since April 1973 at about monthly intervals. Results of analyses available thus far are given in Table 6.
Surface water stations, SW-1 through SW-7, were established as quality and streamflow stations in March, 1975. Quality samples from these stations have been collected twice during spring runoff, once during a May storm event, once during low-flow conditions, and once again in the fall. These data are given in Tables 7 and 8.
Monitoring wells were initially installed on Tract III beginning in July, 1973, by the Montana Bureau of Mines and Geology, additional wells were installed on both tracts by Dames & Moore during the spring and summer of 1975. Wells have been monitored at varying intervals for water level and water quality. Westmoreland Resources plans to continue this program concentrating on wells adjacent to active mining areas.
